## PSY 0210 extension: conditions-validation script

*(0110 students: optional/ungraded — feel free to attempt this for practice, but it is not required and does not affect your grade.)*

Per class04, write a **standalone Python script** that validates your own conditions spreadsheet against this course's ≥18-observations-per-condition rule. This is not a Builder file, not a Colab notebook; you'll run it in PsychoPy's Coder view.

**Start from the template, don't write this from scratch.** Download `hw2/check_conditions_template.py`, save it as `check_conditions.py` in the same folder as your task and conditions file, and open it in Coder. The top of the file has four settings to change to match your task: your conditions file's name, its condition column, your loop's nReps, and the minimum of 18. (This should be the conditions file that you use in the main task loop.) The next part is already written for you; it picks which file to check and reads your condition column into a plain list. You fill in the two parts marked `YOUR PART`:

1.  **Part 1:** count how many rows each condition has, using the counting-dictionary pattern from Think Python ch. 10 and the class04 Colab warm-up.

2.  **Part 2:** inside the loop that's already started for you, use `if`/`else` to print one pass/fail line per condition, e.g.:

    ```         
    Condition 1 has 18 trials - OK
    Condition 0 has 12 trials - FAILS minimum of 18
    ```

Click **Run** in Coder to test it on your own conditions file.

**Submit it as `hw2/task/check_conditions.py`**, uploaded along with the rest of your task. (This exact filename and path is what the automated check looks for; if you name it something else, the 0210 portion of the check will simply be skipped, so use this path.)

The automated check runs your script against a small synthetic sample conditions file (not your real data) and only confirms it runs without crashing and prints output; it does not check your exact wording or verify whether your pass/fail logic is correct. The sample file has the same columns as the original Stroop task's conditions file (`word`, `letterColor`, `corrAns`, `congruent`, plus a `condition` column), so as long as your `CONDITION_COLUMN` is one of those names the sample will have it; if your own conditions file uses a column name of your own invention, the automated check can't find that column and will report a red X even though your script may be fine. If this is true for you, please mention that in your reflection and don't worry about it. One more rule: **print your pass/fail lines rather than stopping the script with an error**. The sample file deliberately contains a failing condition, and the automated check treats an error as a crash. Getting the logic right against your own real conditions file is on you; test it yourself before submitting.
